Legs.Subject: the default surface speaks the BCL unsigned grammar: '+1' answers one and '-0' answers Zero on all eight entry points, while a negative MAGNITUDE ('-1', '-0.00001') is refused — folded into this surface's single FormatException verdict — where the styles surface reports the same two as OverflowException

the two surfaces DIVERGE at the exact top of the range, which is what the rejectExactOutOfRange flag exists for: the exact rendering of MaxValue is accepted by both, while the same literal carrying one further non-zero digit is REFUSED by the default surface and ACCEPTED as MaxValue by the styles surface, because only the default surface tests the prefix numerator against the maximum BEFORE rounding

the surfaces diverge across the whole BOTTOM band (−2⁻¹⁷, 0) by the same mechanism: the default surface refuses '-0.000007' and the exact half-ULP '-0.00000762939453125' (which ties to even onto raw zero) before rounding, while the styles surface rounds first and ANSWERS Zero for both with no OverflowException at all — and '-1e-30' under NumberStyles.Float succeeds as Zero the same way — where '-0.00001', the first magnitude whose rounding is nonzero, is refused by BOTH surfaces; this is the divergence the wing README's Text paragraph now names at both ends

out-of-range and malformed text are refused with the documented distinction: the default surface reports EVERY refusal as a FormatException, while the styles surface separates an out-of-range value (OverflowException) from unparseable text (FormatException); a null string raises an ArgumentNullException naming 's' from both string overloads, and TryParse returns false leaving the default value in every one of those cases

the styled Parse preserves the decimal-overflow distinction its own comment claims: a literal above decimal.MaxValue surfaces as an OverflowException from the RE-ENTERED platform parser rather than as a FormatException, even though the exact pass classified it as merely invalid
